flux-line shear, rather than the breaking of pinning sites, determines the critical current density in superconductors.

flux-lattice shear is the limiting mechanism in high-temperature superconductors (HTS) and that it is the pinning of flux lines that limits J/sub c/ in low-temperature superconducting (LTS) materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the factors which determine whether pin breaking or flux-lattice shear limits the critical current densities of superconductors, and with the consequences for J/sub c/ of the presence of thermal activation in flux-line motion.
the determination of those factors which control the critical current density J/sub c/ of superconducting materials.
the development of a quantitative understanding of the flux-line pinning mechanisms and flux-line lattice plasticity in superconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
flux creep is the dominant factor in limiting critical current density at high magnetic fields, but that the flux lattice shear strength is the dominant factor at low fields.

the critical current density in high- T/sub c/ superconductors is determined by the weakest pinning sites in a flux-line lattice, which are the weakest at the lowest temperatures and at low applied magnetic fields.

the critical current density J/sub c/ in a superconductor depends upon a variety of material and experimental factors and that it can be described by an empirical relation of the type J/sub c/ = f(H, T, E, B, etc.) where H is the applied magnetic field, T is the temperature, E is the applied electric field, B is the magnetic induction, and etc. are various other parameters which are dependent upon the material and experimental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing the theory of flux creep in superconductors.
the critical current density J/sub c/ is determined primarily by the shear strength of flux-line lattice, and that the pinning strength is a secondary factor.
the flux lattice is a plastic material, and that the plasticity theory of metals can be used to describe the flux-lattice shear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flux-lattice shear is a more likely source of flux pinning in the low-field limit, whereas flux pin breaking becomes the limiting factor in the high-field regime.
, in general, pinning will limit J/sub c/ when pinning is strong, and flux-lattice shear will limit J/sub 0/ when pinning becomes weak and the FLL becomes soft.
